notFound.title: Page not found

login.title: Sign in

login.failed: The email or password is incorrect.
login.throttled: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}.

signup.closed: Sign-up is closed on this server. Ask the operator for an account.
signup.emailTaken: An account with this email already exists.

setup.title: Set up Aruma
setup.lead: Create the first account on this server. It will own the first projects.
setup.codeHint: The one-time code is printed in the server log when it starts (the "code" field).
setup.codeRequired: Enter the setup code from the server log.
setup.codeRejected: This code is invalid or was already used. Restarting the server prints a new one.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Each project holds apps, API keys and service accounts.
projects.emptyBody: Create a project, then register your Android, iOS or web apps in it.
projects.noMatchBody: Try another name, ID or number.

newProject.title: New project
newProject.name: Project name
newProject.nameHint: Shown in the console. You can change it later.
newProject.idRules: 6–30 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. Starts with a letter; doesn't end with a hyphen.
newProject.idTaken: This ID is taken. IDs are never reused, even after a project is deleted.
newProject.idPermanent: The project ID goes into your apps' config files and can never be changed.

project.deletedBody: Its apps no longer work. Restore it before {date}; after that it's removed permanently.

overview.subtitle: Project overview
overview.appsHint: Register each app that uses this project, then download its config file.
overview.noAppsBody: Add an Android, iOS or web app to get its config file.
overview.servicesHint: Authentication is ready; the other services arrive in later releases.

flutter.title: Flutter
flutter.description: Generate firebase_options.dart from one registered app per platform.
flutter.placement: Save the file as lib/firebase_options.dart, then initialize the SDK before runApp():

newApp.title: Add an app
newApp.subtitle: Register an app in {project}.
newApp.platformLabel: Which platform is the app for?

platformHint.web: Browser apps, with the JavaScript SDK.
platformHint.android: Android apps, identified by package name.
platformHint.ios: iOS apps, identified by bundle ID.

newApp.permanentAndroid: The package name ties the app to this registration. Enter exactly the applicationId from your build.gradle.
newApp.permanentIos: The bundle ID ties the app to this registration. Enter exactly the bundle identifier from your Xcode target.
newApp.packageTaken: An Android app with this package name already exists in the project.
newApp.bundleTaken: An iOS app with this bundle ID already exists in the project.
newApp.nicknameHint: Optional. Only shown in the console.
newApp.doneBody: The app is registered. Its app ID is

config.androidShared: google-services.json holds every Android app in the project, so one file serves all of them.
config.android1: Move <file>google-services.json</file> into your app module's directory (usually app/).
config.android2: Apply the Google services Gradle plugin, which reads <file>google-services.json</file> at build time.
config.ios1: Drag <file>GoogleService-Info.plist</file> into the root of your Xcode project and add it to every target.
config.web2: Add the configuration below to your app and initialize it.

app.title: App
app.deleteBody: Its config files stop working. You can restore the app within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}; after that it's removed permanently.
app.deletedBody: Restore it before {date}; after that it's removed permanently.
app.configHint: Download it again whenever you need it; it is generated fresh each time.

sha.title: SHA certificate fingerprints
sha.description: Fingerprints of the certificates that sign this Android app.
sha.hint: A SHA-1 or SHA-256 fingerprint, with or without colons.
sha.duplicate: This fingerprint is already registered for the app.
sha.howTo: How do I find my fingerprint?
sha.removeBody: Builds signed with this certificate will no longer match the app.

keys.title: API keys
keys.subtitle: Keys identify this project to the client SDKs.
keys.notSecretTitle: An API key is not a secret
keys.notSecretBody: API keys ship inside your apps and anyone can read them. They identify the project; they don't grant administrative access. Use restrictions to limit where a key is accepted.
keys.emptyBody: A key is created automatically with the first app of each platform.
keys.name: Name
keys.nameHint: Optional. Only shown in the console.
keys.rotateBody: A new key takes over this key's platform: config files you download from now on carry the new key.
keys.rotateOldKey: The old key keeps working until you disable it, so apps already released keep running while you update them.
keys.rotated: New key created. Disable the old one once your apps use the new key.
keys.disableBody: Every request that presents this key will be refused, including from apps already released. You can enable it again.

kindHint.none: The key is accepted from anywhere.
kindHint.browser: Accept the key only from these websites (the Referer header browsers send).
kindHint.ip: Accept the key only from these server addresses. Behind a reverse proxy, list the proxy in trusted_proxies so the client's address is known.
kindHint.android: Accept the key only from these Android apps.
kindHint.ios: Accept the key only from these iOS apps.

summary.ip: {count, plural, one {# IP address} other {# IP addresses}}
summary.android: {count, plural, one {# Android app} other {# Android apps}}
summary.ios: {count, plural, one {# iOS app} other {# iOS apps}}

keys.referrersHint: One per line, such as example.com/* and *.example.com/*. A * may only stand for a subdomain or end the path. Also list the host that serves Aruma's sign-in and email action pages.
keys.needOne: Add at least one entry, or choose no restriction.
keys.badBundleId: Each bundle ID must look like com.example.app.
keys.badReferrer: A website looks like example.com, *.example.com/* or https://example.com:8080/path; a * may only stand for a subdomain or end the path.
keys.badIp: Each entry must be an IPv4 or IPv6 address or a CIDR range such as 198.51.100.0/24.

problem.empty: Add at least one app, or choose no restriction.
problem.packageName: Each package name must look like com.example.app.
problem.sha1: Each app needs a SHA-1 fingerprint (40 hex digits).

keys.apiTargets: Also limited to these APIs (set through the console API):

serviceAccounts.title: Service accounts
serviceAccounts.subtitle: Service accounts let your servers manage the project through the Admin SDK.
serviceAccounts.accountIdHint: 6–30 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. It becomes the first part of the account's email.
serviceAccounts.idTaken: A service account with this ID already exists in the project.
serviceAccounts.emptyBody: Create one for each server or tool that needs administrative access.
serviceAccounts.noKeys: No keys. Generate one to use this account from a server.
serviceAccounts.generateBody: A JSON key file is downloaded to this device.
serviceAccounts.onceBody: Aruma doesn't keep the private key, so the file can't be downloaded again. Store it safely; anyone who has it can act as this service account.
serviceAccounts.keyLimit: This account has the maximum of {max} keys. Delete one to generate another.
serviceAccounts.deleteKeyBody: Servers using this key file lose access at once.
serviceAccounts.deleteBody: {email} and all its keys and tokens stop working at once. This can't be undone.

settings.title: Project settings
settings.name: Project name
settings.authDomainHint: The host name written into config files as authDomain.
settings.dangerBody: Deleting stops every app in the project. You can restore the project for a limited time.
settings.deleteBody: Its apps, keys and service accounts stop working. You can restore it within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, until {date}; after that it's removed permanently.
settings.deleteIdReserved: The project ID stays reserved and can never be used again.
settings.deleted: Project deleted. You can restore it from the banner above.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subtitle: Every change to the project, newest first.
audit.emptyBody: Changes to the project will appear here.
audit.noMatchBody: No loaded entry has this action.
audit.noMatchMore: None of the loaded entries has this action. Load older entries to search further.

account.title: Account
account.languageHint: The console's language on every device you sign in from.
account.passwordHint: Changing the password signs out every other session and revokes all your CLI tokens.
account.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other sessions were signed out and CLI tokens revoked.
account.sessionsHint: Browsers signed in to your account.
account.revokeBody: {device} will need to sign in again.

tokens.title: CLI tokens
tokens.description: Personal tokens for scripts and command-line tools. They act as you, except for account security settings.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: What the token is for, such as “deploy script”.
tokens.passwordHint: Confirm it's you: the token can act on all your projects.
tokens.onceBody: This is the only time the token is shown. Aruma stores only a fingerprint of it.
tokens.usage: Send it in the Authorization header:

limits.title: v1 limits
limits.subtitle: What this release of Aruma supports.
limits.retention: Restore window for deleted projects and apps
limits.noteSingle: Aruma v1 runs as a single server with one database. There is no clustering or failover.
limits.noteRetention: Deleted projects and apps can be restored for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, then they are removed permanently. Project IDs are never reused.
limits.noteKeys: Each service account can hold at most {max, plural, one {# key} other {# keys}} at a time.

section.title: Authentication
section.subtitle: Who can sign in to your apps, and how.

users.title: Users
users.noMatchBody: Search matches the start of an email address, or a whole UID.
users.emptyBody: Users appear here when they sign up in your apps, or when you add one.

create.title: Add user
create.passwordHint: It must meet this project's password policy. Share it with the user over a safe channel.
create.uidHint: Optional. Leave empty to generate one.

user.title: User
user.enabled: User enabled. They can sign in again.
user.methodsHint: Each method the user can sign in with, and the email it carries.
user.noMethods: None. This user signed in anonymously.
user.disableBody: They can't sign in or refresh their session until you enable them again. Their data is kept.
user.revokeBody: Every session ends: apps must sign in again. ID tokens already issued stop passing revocation checks.
user.revoked: The user was signed out everywhere.
user.deleteBody: The account and its sign-in methods are deleted for good. Their sessions end at once.
user.resetBody: A link to choose a new password goes to {email}. It works once, for an hour.

claims.title: Custom claims
claims.description: A JSON object added to the user's ID tokens, for roles and access rules. Changes appear when the user's token next refreshes.
claims.label: Claims (JSON)
claims.saved: Custom claims saved. They appear in the user's next ID token.
claims.reserved: "{name}" is reserved for the ID token. Use another name.

problem.object: Use a JSON object: names and values inside curly braces.
problem.size: Too long: claims can be at most 1000 bytes of compact JSON.

methods.title: Sign-in methods
methods.providersHint: Turn on the ways users can sign in from your apps.
methods.passwordHint: Users sign up and sign in with an email address and a password.
methods.anonymousHint: Users start without an account and can link one later, keeping their UID.
methods.enumerationHint: Sign-in and reset requests answer the same way whether or not an email is registered.
methods.blockSignupHint: Only this console and the Admin SDK can create users. Existing users still sign in.

federated.googleHint: Sign in with a Google account. Create an OAuth client of type Web application in Google Cloud.
federated.appleHint: Sign in with Apple. Create a Services ID and a key for Sign in with Apple in your Apple developer account.
federated.secretSaved: Saved. It is never shown again; enter a new value only to replace it.
federated.redirectHint: Register this address as the authorized redirect URI of your Google OAuth client and as the Return URL of your Apple Services ID.
federated.appleId: 10 uppercase letters or digits, as Apple shows it.
federated.privateKeyFormat: Paste the whole .p8 file, from -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- to the end.
federated.servicesIdHint: The identifier of your Services ID, such as com.example.web.

domains.title: Authorized domains
domains.description: Sign-in pages, redirects and email links work only on these domains.
domains.empty: No authorized domains. Add the domains your apps run on.
domains.invalid: Enter a host name, such as app.example.com, without https:// or a path.
domains.duplicate: This domain is already in the list.

policy.title: Password policy
policy.description: Rules for new passwords: at sign-up, on password change and when you add a user.
policy.enforcementOffHint: Only the minimum length is checked.
policy.enforcementOnHint: Passwords must include every character type chosen below.

templates.title: Email templates
templates.description: What Auth emails say, in each language. The user's language decides which one is sent.
templates.subject: Subject
templates.resetBody: Your changes to this email in this language are discarded and the default text is used again.
templates.needsLink: The message must contain %LINK%, where the action link goes.

appName.title: App name
appName.description: Replaces %APP_NAME% in every email. Empty uses the project name.
appName.label: App name

smtp.title: SMTP server
smtp.description: The mail server Auth sends email through.
smtp.passwordSaved: Saved. It is never shown again; enter a new value only to replace it.
smtp.testBody: Aruma sends a short message through the saved settings.
smtp.devMailbox: Keep email in the dev mailbox
smtp.devMailboxHint: For development: nothing is sent; messages appear on the Mailbox tab.
smtp.devMailboxOn: Email goes to the dev mailbox, not to this server.
smtp.removePasswordBody: Aruma will sign in to the mail server without a password, or not at all.
smtp.testInMailbox: Test email placed in the dev mailbox.

mailbox.title: Mailbox
mailbox.offBody: This server sends Auth email through SMTP. The dev mailbox exists only on development setups.
mailbox.devBody: Email is kept here instead of being sent. Open a link to complete the action as the user would.
mailbox.clearBody: Every message here is deleted. Links in them keep working until they expire.
mailbox.emptyBody: Verification, reset and change emails appear here.
mailbox.subject: Subject
mailbox.smtpBody: New messages are sent through the SMTP server. The ones below were kept earlier.

settings.title: Auth settings
settings.keysHint: Keys rotate on their own {days, plural, one {every day} other {every # days}}. A retired key keeps verifying the tokens it signed until they expire.
settings.noKeys: No keys yet. They are created when the project issues its first token.
settings.rotateBody: The next key starts signing. Tokens already issued keep working until they expire, so nobody is signed out.
settings.emergencyWarning: Use this only if a key may have leaked.
settings.emergencyBody: The active key is destroyed. Aruma refuses the tokens it signed at once; servers that verify tokens themselves stop accepting them within a minute, when their cached key list expires. Users must refresh or sign in again.
settings.limitsHint: Fixed by the server; no setting changes them.
settings.perMinute: {count} a minute per address, bursts of up to {burst}
settings.failures: After {count, plural, one {# wrong password} other {# wrong passwords}} within {window}, each attempt waits longer, up to {max}.
